case_name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India

pages.text:
REPORTABLE
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
WRIT PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 167 OF 2012

SHREYA SINGHAL ... PETITIONER
VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA ... RESPONDENT

JUDGMENT

R.F. NARIMAN, J.

1. This batch of writ petitions raises questions of great constitutional importance touching upon the fundamental right of free speech and expression guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India. The primary challenge is directed against Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

2. Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 penalizes the sending of offensive messages through communication services. We find that the terms used in Section 66A such as 'offensive' and 'annoyance' are vague, nebulous, and lack clear judicial definition, creating an impermissible chilling effect on speech.

3. Consequently, Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 is declared unconstitutional in its entirety as being violative of Article 19(1)(a) and not saved under Article 19(2). However, provisions dealing with cyber offenses, identity theft under Section 66C, and cheating by personation under Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000 remain valid and enforceable.
